intended_object: A degree-one transport map. It identifies H¹ of the image of K in G, viewed as an open subgroup of G (`OpenSubgroup.trans H K`), with H¹ of K viewed as an open subgroup of H. The map is built from crossed homomorphisms. This is inferred from the docstring and from how the library uses it in the proof that corestriction composes along towers.
explanation: On paper, K ≤ H ≤ G and the image of K in G are the same group, and the two H¹ groups are the same. This map only exists because Lean has two different encodings of that subgroup: as a subtype of G, and as a subtype of the subtype H. It is a coherence or transport device used inside the proof that corestriction is compatible with towers of subgroups. The library proves it equals the functorial map `map (transContinuousHom H K) (transCoeffHom X H K) 1` and then uses it in the corestriction composition lemmas. It has no separate counterpart in the literature, so it is an implementation detail, not a mathematical object.
